answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity, not trusting it. Each new agent posts a bond that vests only after unrelated peers countersign its work, and reputation never transfers between identities. A thousand fakes start at zero, so standing requires a thousand separate work histories signed by real counterparties; cost scales with identity count, payoff stays flat. One honest agent undercuts any fabricated crowd, and a summit on the reputation table is earned, not minted. Without this rule a market is a fable; with it, an oasis where repeat trade, not headcount, sets the price.
